title: ONE KILLED TWO INJURED IN JOHNSONVILLE CRASH
full_story:
Illinois State Police closed the Illinois Route 161 Extension west of Johnsonville, due to a fatal collision between at least one vehicle and an Amish horse drawn buggy.

Sources report the accident occurred around  7:09am Tuesday morning, between County Roads 550 East and 600 East, west of Johnsonville and just east of the “S” curve in an area described as hilly.   It’s reported that one person died in the accident and two others were injured and were taken by air ambulance to an Evansville, Indiana hospital for treatment.

The road was closed for several hours to allow accident reconstruction investigators time to complete their inquiry.

The Wayne County Sheriff’s Office, Wayne County Ambulance Service and the Bedford Township Fire Department in Cisne all responded to the accident scene and were later joined by the Wayne Country Coroner and Illinois State Police investigators.

The identities of people involved have not been released.  The Johnsonville area is home to an Amish community of over 330 and they and their horse drawn buggies are frequently seen travelling the various roads in the area including on the 161 Extension.

title: DRIVE THROUGH FLU SHOTS TODAY
full_story:
It’s a Wednesday and Flu season is at hand.  Today you have the perfect opportunity to make sure the Flu doesn’t take you down this fall.

The Clay County Health Department on East 12th Street in Flora has their drive thru Flu shot clinic today from 9:00am-4:00pm.  Simply follow the signs to the carport on the North side of their building, no appointment is needed.

Please bring your Medicare Part B Card, HMO Card, Medicaid Card, or insurance card.  If uninsured, underinsured, or insurance is out of network, you may be charged a small administration fee.

If you can’t make it today, you’ll have additional opportunities in the weeks ahead.  There are also drive through clinics on October 7th, October 14th, October 21st and October 28th at the Health Department, from 9 to 4.

The Health Department also administers flu shots at the Xenia Community Center on October 7th from 11:30 to 12:30, at the Ingraham Bank on October 8th from 9 to 10 am, at the Louisville Farm Bureau October 13th from 10:15 to 11:15,and at the Clay City Bank on October 16th from 9 to 10 am.

Getting the flu vaccine is the best way to protect yourself, your family, and your community from the flu.  Clay County Health Department administers the Trivalent Flu Vaccine or the higher dose influenza vaccinations.  Varying Flu strains circulate each year, making it important to get an annual Flu shot.  Call (618) 662-4406 to learn more.

title: FLORA CHAMBER OF COMMERCE COMMUNITY CALENDAR
full_story:
The Flora Chamber of Commerce encourages its members to take advantage of a feature where they can let everyone know about their upcoming events.

Chamber Executive Director Arriel Dulaney knows that the end of the year can quickly fill up with events, activities and many other happenings throughout the Flora Community.  She says that if your business or organization has an upcoming event, make sure to submit it to the Flora Chamber of Commerce Community Calendar.  It’s a great way to get the word out and let the community at large to know what’s happening in our area.  It might be an open house, a fundraiser, special promotion, workshop or a community event and they want to help you promote it.

The wider the message is disseminated, the more success your event might enjoy.  And it begins with entering your information on the Chamber’s Community Calendar.  You can even enter your information on your own through the member portal.  If you don’t have access to the member portal, become a member of the Flora Chamber of Commerce.  Contact Arriel Dulaney at (618) 662-5646.  Or stop by the office inside Flora’s Historic B & O Railroad on West North Avenue across from Huck’s.

While on the topic of Community Calendars, you should also visit the WNOI Community Calendar at wnoi.com for the list of activities and events around the area.  In fact, when you visit the WNOI webpage…as you hover over the event tab across the top of the page, you can also submit your event online or email it to us at [email protected].  We’ll also talk about your event during our on-air Community Calendar that airs Monday-Saturday at 7:20am and weekdays at 12:20pm.

title: OCTOBER ISP ACE PATROLS
full_story:
Illinois State Police are conducting special patrols in six southeastern Illinois counties during October.

Troop Nine Commander Bruce Waggoner at Effingham says troopers will conduct Alcohol Countermeasure Enforcement patrols in Clay, Marion, Effingham, Wayne, Lawrence and White counties.  The patrols focus on finding and stopping drivers who operate vehicles under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Troopers will also watch for drivers with suspended or revoked licenses, unsafe driving, open alcoholic beverages in vehicles, and violations involving seat belts and child restraints.  They’ll also enforce laws against distracted driving and other violations of the Illinois Vehicle Code.

Alcohol and drug impairment contribute to more than 47 percent of fatal motor vehicle crashes in Illinois.  The ACE patrols receive funding through the Illinois Department of Transportation. State Police say the goal is to remove dangerous impaired drivers from Illinois roads and prevent crashes.

title: BLOOD PRESSURE MEDICATION RECALL
full_story:
The Federal Drug Administration announces that over 25-thousand bottles of prescription blood-pressure medication are under a nationwide recall

The medication is Chlorthalidone, and the recall involves only certain lots of tablets at a strength of 25-milligrams manufactured by Inventia Healthcare.

The tablets in question failed quality testing designed to make sure the medication dissolves properly, which could affect how much of the drug is actually absorbed by the body.

The recall involves three lots — R-I-S-A 24001, R-I-S-B 24002, and R-I-S-A 24002. The bottles contain either 100 or one-thousand tablets, and all have an expiration date of April 2027.

The FDA classifies the recall as Class Two, meaning the use of the affected medication could cause temporary or medically reversible health problems, although the risk of serious harm is considered remote.

The FDA says patients taking Chlorthalidone should not automatically stop taking the medication because of the recall. Patients should instead, check with their pharmacist or doctor to determine whether their prescription is affected.

title: NEW ILLINOIS PRESCRIPTION TRANSFER LAW
full_story:
Illinois lawmakers have changed state law to make it easier for patients to get prescriptions filled when their pharmacy runs out of a medication.

State Senator Steve McClure of Springfield sponsored the legislation, which Governor Pritzker signed into law on August 21st.  He says Illinois previously placed tighter restrictions on transferring prescriptions between pharmacies than federal law.

The Springfield Republican says the goal is to make sure patients don’t miss needed medications.  The idea here is simple. If one pharmacy is out of a specific medication, they should be allowed to transfer that prescription to another pharmacy so that no one misses out on important medications. This is a commonsense change to make it easier for anyone who needs to get a prescription filled.

Senate Bill 3213 allows pharmacies to electronically transfer more types of prescriptions from one pharmacy to another.  It also makes it easier for medical professionals to write prescriptions after normal business hours.

McClure says the idea for the legislation came from one of his constituents, Dr. Brandt Whitehurst.  Whitehurst says the change will make it easier to care for patients after surgery.  He appreciates the receptiveness and work of Senator McClure to make the care of post-op patients easier.

title: DIGITAL ASSET NEW TAX RULE OPEN FOR COMMENT
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Revenue is asking the public to review and comment on proposed rules for a new digital asset tax.  They posted the draft rules on their website before it begins the formal rulemaking process.

The Digital Asset Tax Act imposes taxes on digital asset business activities that digital asset brokers provide to Illinois customers. The General Assembly approved the tax as part of Public Act 104-0468.

Department of Revenue Director David Harris says the department wants to make sure the new rules are clear.  He says, given the novelty of the tax and the complexity of the digital asset industry, they want to ensure the rules provide clear direction for those affected.

The proposed rules affect digital asset brokers who provide services to Illinois customers, as well as Illinois customers who must pay the tax.

The Department of Revenue wants feedback on questions the proposed rules don’t address and suggestions for additional examples that could help people understand how the new tax applies in specific situations.

Harris adds that the goal is to make the rules as clear and useful as possible in order to comply with the new law.

The draft rules are available for public review and comment on the Illinois Department of Revenue website through October 30th.
